claim: The PubMed abstract for an observational workflow time study reports doctors in the emergency department of one large Australian hospital observed for 121.7 hours across 58 sessions. It conceptualised interruptive events as prompts and coded doctors' responses as task-switching, multitasking, acknowledgement, deferral, and deflection. Prompt rates varied by work scenario; response strategy varied with task type, prompt type, and department location, and task-switching was the most frequent reported strategy. The abstract does not report a complete eligible-action choice set, event denominator, portable transition probability, or universal task-selection policy; these remain unknown.
